Nearly all developed countries have universal healthcare, and even those that don't have Medicare for the elderly.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Also, the customers are looking at pictures of their new bodies, presumably ones taken during the fashion shows. Does that not tip them off that these were real people, and not vatgrown husks?

The assumption I had (before I figured out the twist) was that it was a picture of their first customer for that particular "model" (maybe even a "beta tester" or w/e). Or maybe CGI's gotten advanced enough that you could pass off a real photo as a CGI model.

The main problem I had was that someone, at some point, might notice that they only ever use each "model" once. Like, if you're just buying one body for the rest of your life, sure, but what if you want to tell a friend about the service and you notice that your body type is unavailable? Or what if you get in a really bad accident that you can't recover from and just want to be transferred into another instance of the same body type?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I liked this tale, but there is a bit of fridge logic that makes it somewhat implausible.

I don't think this company would be able to keep the fact that these bodies aren't clones secret for very long, as a body that's been lived in for even just a couple decades would be significantly different from one fresh out of a cloning vat (This is a criticism that some people brought up for the movie Self/less, by the way).

Now I get that a lot of people wouldn't want to do their due diligence and just accept a new body a face value, but surely some people would look into this and realize they can't possibly be growing these bodies from vats.

Also, the customers are looking at pictures of their new bodies, presumably ones taken during the fashion shows. Does that not tip them off that these were real people, and not vatgrown husks?

I've already mentioned this in another Omega-k entry (the PL format), but in this situation, it really doesn't make sense that SENS and regenerative medicine aren't more advanced. I get that you're going for body horror, but can't they just us a bioprinter to make Kira's mom a new heart? And don't tell me it's because they can't afford it. Nearly all developed countries have universal healthcare, and even those that don't have Medicare for the elderly.

Sorry to rant. I like this tale, and I like this series, it's just that some of the more horrific aspects of it feel unrealistically bad.
